episode_title: Dr. Preston Cherry: Can AI Fake What Makes a Great Advisor?

real_qa.q: How can financial advisors build trust with clients in an AI world when AI can make anyone sound articulate and knowledgeable?
real_qa.r: Advisors must take the extra step to craft, lead, and shape AI output by inserting their own knowledge, wisdom, and judgment into what AI produces. Trust is built through a track record of behavior and the ability to follow up, follow through, and deliver at a high level on what you've communicated. It requires demonstrating that you can interpret financial reality and provide discernment and conviction that AI alone cannot deliver—clients want to be led by someone who genuinely understands their situation, not just someone who sounds smart.
real_qa.requete: how advisors build trust AI world

real_qa.q: What must financial advisors do differently to demonstrate they provide value that AI cannot replicate?
real_qa.r: Advisors must go beyond accepting AI-generated content at face value and inject their 20 years of expertise, client relationships, lived experience, and craft knowledge into that output. When clients read personalized content, they should feel it answers their specific question at a deeper level with interconnected experiences and information tailored to their needs. This differentiation comes from the advisor's willingness to review, curate, and transform AI output rather than deploying it as-is, building earned trust through demonstrated expertise.
real_qa.requete: financial advisor value AI cannot do

real_qa.q: How does understanding a client move beyond having access to all their factual information in an AI-driven advisory practice?
real_qa.r: Having facts about a client—birthdays, anniversaries, quantitative and qualitative data—is one thing, but understanding what those facts mean to that specific person is entirely different. This requires 'financial reality interpreted' through discernment, conviction, and decisive clarity. The advisor must take all the organized information AI provides and synthesize it through judgment to help the client feel understood, not just informed. This interpretive layer is what clients truly seek when they engage an advisor.

real_qa.q: What skills should young financial advisors prioritize to remain valuable in an AI-enabled industry?
real_qa.r: Young advisors must pair their natural technological proficiency with fundamental domain knowledge in wealth management, client experience, investment management, and estate planning. More critically, they must develop the ability to interpret information, make judgments, exercise discernment, and make decisions independently rather than always requiring someone else to interpret for them. If you cannot assess what's happening inside a firm, understand how it serves clients, and contribute original thinking, your value is diminished regardless of AI capability. The combination of technical skill, domain expertise, and interpretive judgment is what creates tremendous value.

real_qa.q: What is the most difficult skill for financial advisors to develop and maintain as AI transforms advisory practice?
real_qa.r: Being vulnerable and having the courage to open yourself up to constant coaching and criticism in order to improve is critical. This means anonymizing client conversations, scoring your own performance against established formats and guardrails, identifying gaps, and being willing to acknowledge when you fall short—such as over-speaking, over-convincing, or deviating from your system. Advisors must pair this vulnerability with the discipline to follow the systems and protocols they've built, and cross-reference their performance against multiple AI platforms like Claude and ChatGPT to gain objective feedback on how to serve clients better.

guest.bio_context: Dr. Preston Cherry is a financial advisor with decades of experience bridging the pre-AI and AI eras in wealth management. He has worked extensively with younger advisors as a coach and trainer, and previously served as a professor. He specializes in serving executives in the oil and gas sector and has developed AI-driven workflows and agent systems to optimize both client experience and advisory team performance.
